chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who travels during the month of Ramadan, whether he should fast or break his fast: He said, 'If he departs before midday, let him break his fast; and if he departs after midday, let him fast.' And he said, 'This is recognized by the words of Ali (peace be upon him): I fast and I break until when the sun declines, determination is made upon me,' meaning the fasting.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler in Ramadan who leaves after dawn: do they break or complete their fast?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific legal status of a traveler who departs after dawn, establishing that the 'determination' (‘azm) to fast occurs at midday (Zawal), a principle derived from Imam Ali’s practice. Consequently, if one leaves before Zawal, the fast is broken without needing to make it up as a traveler; if after Zawal, the fast is completed and later compensated. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the timing of intention relative to the physical act of travel during Ramadan.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who travels during a Month of Ramazan, should he be Fasting or breaking?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he goes out before the midday, so let him break, and if he goes out after the midday, so let him Fast’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is recognised by the words of Ali<sup>asws</sup>: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> Fast and I<sup>asws</sup> break until when the sun (starts the) decline, being Determined upon me<sup>asws</sup>’, meaning the Fasts’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who travels in the month of Ramadan, if he is required to fast or stop fasting. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he goes out before Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime), he stops fasting; and if he goes out after Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime), then he fasts.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘This comes from the words of Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that say, “I fast and stop fasting until it is Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime), thereafter it is definitely obligatory on me, meaning thereby fasting.’””
